policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV JDG.9.8 renders the clause as 'Reign thou over us,' which does not distinguish the qere מָלְכָ֥ה from the ketiv מלוכה; no mapped textual note is given, so both readings remain compatible and the documented qere base remains the fallback.

ASV JDG.9.12 renders the clause as 'reign over us,' which does not distinguish the qere מָלְכִ֥י from the ketiv מלוכי; no mapped textual note is given, so both readings remain compatible and the documented qere base remains the fallback.
